why: A run-length scan whose only trap is the tie rule: compare with >= so a later run of equal length replaces the earlier one, and remember to close the last run after the loop.
hints: Scan the string once, tracking the current run's character and length.
When the character changes (or the string ends), compare the finished run with the best. Which comparison makes the rightmost run win a tie?
Use >= for the update so later equal runs replace earlier ones, and process the final run after the loop. Return char + str(length). O(n).
pitfalls: Forgetting the final run: the longest run is often the last one.
Using > keeps the leftmost run on ties; the problem wants the rightmost.
The count is written in decimal and can have two digits (e.g. 'a12').
